councils.name: City of Darwin

lodgement.label: Lodge with the NT Development Consent Authority on Development Applications Online (DAO)

steps: Check your zone and overlays on NR Maps, then check the NT Planning Scheme 2020 to see if your use is permitted, merit assessable or impact assessable.

If you need a development permit, lodge on Development Applications Online (DAO) with a statement of effect and plans. The NT Government's Development Assessment Services processes it, not the council.
Pay the NT Government application fee (from $269 for a single dwelling) and any advertising fee ($149).
The council is asked to comment as a service authority. Some applications are exhibited for 7, 14 or 28 days.
The Development Consent Authority decides. It takes about 8 weeks. Then get a building permit from a registered building certifier.

pre_lodgement.note: Meet with an NT Government planner before you lodge. The council can advise on its own works and service requirements.

items.label: Development permit, single dwelling on one lot
Change of use, no physical development

NT.GOV.AU: apply for a development permit
Geoscape LGA layer (abb_name field), Australian Government spatial services

gaps: Development applications go to the NT Development Consent Authority, not the council.
No separate planning email; the general council email is used for council matters like driveways, verges and rates.

Council's role is as a service authority: it comments on development applications to the Development Consent Authority and approves works on council roads and drains. Its own planning page wasn't read.

Spatial name is the upper-cased abb_name from the national Geoscape LGA layer (built from NT Government data). The NT Government's own LGA boundaries layer wasn't opened, so the spelling isn't confirmed there.
The Geoscape layer also has a separate 'Darwin Waterfront Precinct' area, which is not part of this council's entry.
